text.headline: A Timeline of the Spider-Man Films
text.text:
From Sam Raimi's 2002 original to Brand New Day (2026), Spider-Man has been rebooted twice in live action and reinvented in animation. This timeline argues that each new version came from a business decision as much as a creative one: who held the film rights, and who Sony partnered with, shaped which Spider-Man audiences got.

The shaded bands at the bottom show each lead actor's run. Slide colors match the four film series, and grey slides show the deals and decisions behind them.

media.caption: The actors who have played Spider-Man on film.
media.alt: A row of the live-action and animated actors who have played Spider-Man, shown side by side.

text.headline: Spider-Man
text.text:
Peter Parker gains spider powers after a radioactive bite and must stop the Green Goblin.

Why it matters: Directed by Sam Raimi and starring Tobey Maguire, it earned about $822 million worldwide. That success helped prove superhero films could be reliable blockbusters, years before the Marvel Cinematic Universe existed.

text.headline: Spider-Man 2
text.text:
Peter struggles to balance his life and his love for Mary Jane while battling Doctor Octopus.

Why it matters: It won the Academy Award for Best Visual Effects and is often ranked among the best superhero films. It earned about $790 million worldwide.

text.headline: Spider-Man 3
text.text:
An alien suit brings out Peter's dark side as he faces Sandman, Harry Osborn, and Venom.

Why it matters: The trilogy's biggest earner, at nearly $900 million worldwide, but critics faulted its crowded cast of villains. That mixed response set up what happened next.

text.headline: Spider-Man 4 is canceled
text.text: Sony and Sam Raimi could not agree on Spider-Man 4 in time for its planned release. Sony canceled it and announced a reboot with a new cast. Sony needed to keep making Spider-Man films so it could keep the film rights it licensed from Marvel.

media.caption: Background on the history of Spider-Man's film rights.

text.headline: The Amazing Spider-Man
text.text:
Peter looks into his parents' disappearance and takes on the Lizard while falling for Gwen Stacy.

Why it matters: Directed by Marc Webb, with Andrew Garfield and Emma Stone, it retold the origin story only ten years after the first one. It earned about $758 million worldwide.

text.headline: The Amazing Spider-Man 2
text.text:
Peter fights Electro and the Green Goblin, and his relationship with Gwen ends in tragedy.

Why it matters: At about $709 million worldwide, it is the lowest-grossing live-action Spider-Man film. Sony dropped its plans for more sequels and spin-offs, including The Sinister Six.

text.headline: Sony and Marvel Studios make a deal
text.text: Sony agreed to share Spider-Man with Marvel Studios. Sony kept the rights and the box office, and Marvel could put the character in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Spider-Man was rebooted for the second time.

media.caption: Background on the Sony–Marvel Studios agreement.

text.headline: Tom Holland debuts in Captain America: Civil War
text.text: Holland's Peter Parker first appears as a supporting character in a Marvel Studios film. This was a year before his own solo film, which skipped the origin story audiences had already seen twice.

text.headline: Spider-Man: Homecoming
text.text:
Teenage Peter tries to impress Tony Stark by stopping the Vulture's alien weapon ring.

Why it matters: Directed by Jon Watts, it was the first solo Spider-Man film set in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. It earned about $880 million worldwide.

text.headline: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
text.text:
Miles Morales teams up with spider people from other dimensions to stop Kingpin.

Why it matters: It won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. Its comic-book art style influenced many animated films that followed, and it made Miles Morales, an Afro-Latino Spider-Man, a lead character on screen.

text.headline: Spider-Man: Far From Home
text.text:
On a school trip to Europe, Peter faces Mysterio, who reveals his identity to the world.

Why it matters: It was the first Spider-Man film to earn more than $1 billion worldwide.

text.headline: Sony and Disney renew the deal
text.text: In August 2019, talks between Sony and Disney broke down, and it looked like Spider-Man would leave the Marvel Cinematic Universe. A month later, the companies agreed on a new deal for a third Holland film, which became No Way Home.

text.headline: Spider-Man: No Way Home
text.text:
A spell by Doctor Strange goes wrong and brings villains and Spider-Men from other universes.

Why it matters: It brought back Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield, joining all three live-action eras in one film. It earned about $1.9 billion worldwide.

text.headline: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
text.text:
Miles clashes with a society of Spider People over what it means to be a hero.

Why it matters: It earned about $690 million worldwide, far more than the first film, and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. It ends on a cliffhanger.

text.headline: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
text.text:
With the world having forgotten Peter Parker, he starts a new chapter as Spider-Man on his own.

Why it matters: Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, it passed $2 billion worldwide in August 2026, making it the highest-grossing Spider-Man film.

text.headline: Coming next: Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse
text.text: The third Spider-Verse film will finish the story Across the Spider-Verse left on a cliffhanger. Its release date has moved several times, so check a current listing.
